prompt: Write an email to a colleague about doing every task well, however small. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Small tasks, done well

Hi Sam,

I've been thinking about something since our project wrapped up last week, and I wanted to share it with you.

When I look back at the work that made the biggest difference, it usually wasn't the big, visible deliverables. It was the small things: the meeting notes that went out the same afternoon, the spreadsheet with clearly labeled columns, the follow-up email that answered the question before anyone had to ask it. None of those tasks took long. But together they made everything else run more smoothly.

I've come to believe that how we handle small tasks is the truest measure of how we work. Nobody is watching closely when we rename a file properly or double-check a figure before sending a report. We could cut a corner and almost certainly get away with it. That's exactly why doing it well matters. It builds a habit, and the habit shows up when the stakes are high.

There's also a practical side. Small sloppy work has a way of compounding. An unlabeled file costs someone ten minutes to figure out. A vague handoff note leads to a clarifying meeting. A typo in a client email chips away at trust, even if only a little. Each one is minor, but they add up to friction, and friction slows the whole team down. On the flip side, careful work compounds in the other direction. People start to rely on you, and that reliability is worth more than almost any single big win.

I don't mean perfectionism. Spending an hour polishing a two-line message isn't the goal, and part of doing a task well is judging how much care it deserves. What I mean is giving each task your full attention for the few minutes it needs. Read it over once before you hit send. Ask yourself whether the next person could pick this up without a question. Finish what you started instead of leaving it at "good enough."

I've tried to hold myself to this lately, and I've noticed two things. My work has fewer do-overs, and I feel better about it. There's a quiet satisfaction in knowing that something is simply done right.

I've also noticed that you already do this. Your documentation on the vendor onboarding was the clearest I've seen here, and it saved me real time. I wanted you to know that people see it, even when it seems nobody is looking.

Maybe we could trade a few thoughts on this over coffee next week. I'd love to hear what small habits have worked for you.

Best,
[name]
